       TEXAS SCOTTISH RITE HOSPITAL FOR CRIPPLED CHILDREN’S
                MOTION TO CONFIRM APPLICABILITY OF
                SOAH ORDER NO. 35 TO DOCKET NO. 59182

                                   I.     INTRODUCTION

       Texas Scottish Rite Hospital for Crippled Children, d/b/a Texas Scottish Rite Hospital for

Children (“TSRH” or the “Hospital”), respectfully moves the Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”)

to confirm that SOAH Order No. 35, filed September 22, 2026, in PUC Docket No. 59475, SOAH




TSRH’s Motion to Confirm Applicability of SOAH Order No. 35 to Docket No. 59182
PUC Docket Nos. 59182 & 59475                                                             Page 1
 Docket No. 473-26-16349, applies equally to parties in PUC Docket No. 59182, SOAH Docket

No. 473-26-10397, and to cause SOAH Order No. 35 to be filed in Docket No. 59182.

        TSRH is an intervenor in Docket No. 59182, having been granted intervention by SOAH

Order No. 9. TSRH participated in the Docket No. 59182 hearing on the merits and filed testimony.

Because the issue of need for the Big Hill Substation to Sand Lake Switch 765-kV transmission

line was consolidated with Docket No. 59475 by joint SOAH Order No. 24, 1 TSRH also appeared

at the Docket No. 59475 evidentiary hearing on the issue of need. This Motion seeks only

confirmation to ensure that Docket No. 59182 parties may participate in the remand on the need

issue on equal footing with Docket No. 59475 parties.

                                                II. ARGUMENT

        On May 8, 2026, the ALJs consolidated Dockets 59182 and 59475 for the limited purpose

of addressing the need for both segments of Import Path 2. SOAH Order No. 24 in Docket No.

59182 and SOAH Order No. 12 in Docket No. 59475 granted consolidation pursuant to PURA §

37.0541, which requires consolidation of transmission-line CCN proceedings when the proposed

lines share a common point of interconnection. The Proposal for Decision (“PFD”) in Docket No.

59182 confirmed that need issues under PURA § 37.056(c)(1)–(2) and (4)(F)—Preliminary Order

Issues 5 through 7—were consolidated with and would be addressed in the PFD for Docket No.

59475. As a result of consolidation, the two proceedings are treated as one on the need issue. Texas

courts distinguish true consolidation from a mere joint hearing or trial; when proceedings are truly

consolidated, the separate matters “become merged and are thereafter treated as one suit” and




1
 See Docket No. 59475, SOAH Order No. 12 (May 8, 2026) (the identical order to SOAH Order No. 24 filed in
Docket No. 59182).

TSRH’s Motion to Confirm Applicability of SOAH Order No. 35 to Docket No. 59182
PUC Docket Nos. 59182 & 59475                                                                         Page 2
 “proceed as a single action.” 2 Because Docket Nos. 59182 and 59475 were consolidated for the

common issue of need, the parties should be afforded the same opportunity to brief and respond

on that consolidated issue, while issues outside the consolidation remain in their respective

dockets.

        On September 18, 2026, the Commission issued its Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH

bearing both docket captions—Docket No. 59182 and Docket No. 59475—and directing the ALJs

to fully address Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13, which concern whether the proposed

transmission facilities are necessary to meet certain reliability standards and the estimated

congestion cost savings for consumers. The remand order expressly recognized that the two

proceedings were consolidated at SOAH on May 8, 2026, to address common issues. 3

        SOAH Order No. 34, issued September 15, 2026 in Docket No. 59475, indicated that the

evidentiary record will not be reopened and that the ALJs will issue a supplemental PFD

addressing only the limited remand issues. SOAH Order No. 35, issued September 22, 2026 in

Docket No. 59475, implements the remand by requiring briefing on Issues 11 and 13, with briefs

due October 7, 2026, and responses due October 19, 2026. SOAH Order No. 35 directs Applicants

and Commission Staff to brief and permits other parties to file briefs and responses.

        However, SOAH Order No. 35 is currently captioned and filed in Docket No. 59475 only.

Because Issues 11 and 13 concern the need for the transmission facilities proposed in both

dockets—issues that were expressly consolidated—the absence of SOAH Order No. 35 from the

Docket No. 59182 record creates an ambiguity regarding whether Docket No. 59182 parties may



2
 Hong Kong Dev., Inc. v. Nguyen, 229 S.W.3d 415, 432–33 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2007, pet. denied)
(quoting Perry v. Del Rio, 53 S.W.3d 818, 825 n.6 (Tex. App.—Austin 2001, pet. dism’d)).
3
 Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH at 2 (Sep. 18, 2026); see also 16 TAC § 22.262(c) (authorizing remand
with or without reopening the hearing); Tex. Gov’t Code § 2003.049(e) (requiring the Commission to provide
SOAH a list of issues upon receiving jurisdiction of a proceeding).

TSRH’s Motion to Confirm Applicability of SOAH Order No. 35 to Docket No. 59182
PUC Docket Nos. 59182 & 59475                                                                         Page 3
 participate in the remand briefing. Fundamental fairness, certain applicable statutes, and the

procedural rules governing these proceedings require that the parties in both proceedings (i.e.,

Docket No. 59182 and Docket No. 59475) whose rights are affected by the consolidated need

determination receive clear notice of, and an equal opportunity to participate in, the remand

proceedings. 4

         Filing SOAH Order No. 35 in Docket No. 59182 ensures that the procedural vehicle

implementing the Commission’s remand—an order that itself bears both docket numbers—is

reflected in both dockets so that all affected intervenors receive proper notice and may brief the

remanded issues on equal footing. 5 Similarly, the deadlines for briefs and responses should be

extended day-for-day to account for the delay in filing SOAH Order No. 35, which is necessary to

ensure that Docket No. 59182 parties receive the same amount of time to prepare and participate

as parties in the remand of the consolidated issues in Docket Nos. 59182 and 59475.

                                                      III. PRAYER

         WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Texas Scottish Rite Hospital for Crippled

Children respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges:

         1. Issue an order confirming that SOAH Order No. 35 applies to Docket No. 59182 and to

parties in Docket No. 59182;

         2. Cause SOAH Order No. 35 to be filed in PUC Docket No. 59182;


4
  See 16 TAC § 22.1 (the purpose of the procedural rules is to “promote the just and efficient disposition of
proceedings and public participation”); 16 TAC § 22.202(c)–(d) (presiding officer shall conduct hearings to secure
fairness and promote development of the record); 1 TAC § 155.3(a), (g) (SOAH rules may be modified to promote
fair and efficient handling and shall be construed to ensure just and expeditious determination); 1 TAC § 155.155(a)
(ALJs may issue orders to control participation requirements and ensure a fair and efficient contested case process).
These CCN cases are contested cases as provided by PURA § 14.053 and Texas Gov’t Code § 2003.049(a). The
Intervenors in Docket 59182 are therefore entitled to present argument on each issue in the case, as provided by the
APA at Texas Gov’t Code 2001.051(2).
5
 See 1 TAC § 155.51(d) (any party may move for appropriate relief after SOAH acquires jurisdiction); 16 TAC §
22.34(a) (consolidation serves efficiency and prevents unwarranted delay without prejudice to parties).

TSRH’s Motion to Confirm Applicability of SOAH Order No. 35 to Docket No. 59182
PUC Docket Nos. 59182 & 59475                                                                                 Page 4
         3. Extend the briefing deadlines established by SOAH Order No. 35 on a day-for-day basis

to account for any delay in filing Order No. 35 in Docket No. 59182; and

        4. Grant TSRH all other and further relief, whether at law or in equity, to which it may

show itself justly entitled.
